dedupe_keys.name: on the importance of internet exchange points for today s internet ecosystem survey of public ixp information chatzis smaragdakis and feldmann 2013

description: This 2013 survey article argues that Internet exchange points deserve more attention from networking researchers. It traces IXPs to the Network Access Points created when NSFNET was decommissioned in 1994 and 1995, notes that more than 300 IXPs were operational worldwide in May 2013 (a public list showed 391, including some not fully operational), and that the largest handle daily traffic comparable to the largest Tier-1 ISPs. The authors survey the existing but little known public sources of information about IXPs to describe technical and operational aspects, highlight differences between regions, especially Europe and North America, and discuss how IXPs connect to data centres, cloud services, software-defined networking and mobile communication, and how IXP-driven innovation in Europe shapes the Internet marketplace. Producer: Chatzis, Smaragdakis and Feldmann, TU Berlin and T-Labs, 2013. Coverage: global, focus on Europe and North America. Access: free arXiv PDF; the abstract and introduction were read. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: figures are from 2013, and it does not cover equipment ageing despite the search that found it. Simulation uses: the description of IXP types and roles gives reference context for network models of interconnection. Related records: the PCH IXP directory (data-pch-ixp-directory) and the Euro-IX IXP database (data-euro-ix-ixp-database).
